messages.content: I shrug “she wants my research, she offered her families archives. I told her I want a date on top of that” I laugh as if I made a joke as we arrive to Harry Fred and George

"You asked *Malfoy* for a—" Hermione stops herself, glances around, and lowers her voice to a hiss. "That wasn't a joke, was it. Seth, her family could buy a wing of St. Mungo's. You're negotiating *archives* against a *dinner*?"

"That's the spirit," Fred says as the group comes together, sliding down the bench to make room. "Lead with audacity, sort terms later. Speaking of audacity — Georgie and I have been scheming since breakfast."

George leans in, lowering his voice theatrically. "Temporary tattoo shop. Speed-dating format. One galleon a design, students queue up, we cash in before anyone thinks to regulate it."

Harry looks up from his plate, bewildered. "Someone want to explain what we're straightening the story about?"
You “Yes. Temporary tattoo shop. I am 100% in. I have a bunch of runes that do silly but fun things.” I say as I sit

"Knew it," Fred says, slapping the bench. "Hear that, Harry? The American's in."

Harry leans around Ron, still lost. "Someone please explain what temporary tattoo shop means."

"Simple," George says, ticking it off on his fingers. "We set up a stall — probably the common room, maybe Hogsmeade if we're feeling brave. Press here supplies the runic designs. Silly ones. Moving tattoos, colour-changing, that sort of thing. One galleon a pop."

"Customers queue up, get inked, walk away delighted," Fred says. "We split proceeds four ways — well, three, if Harry wants in for the labour."

"I don't even know what the labour is yet," Harry protests, but he's grinning now.

"Look," George says, turning to you with genuine curiosity, "how fast can you actually do one? Say — a tattoo that winks when the person lies? Because if it takes you twenty minutes per customer, we're dead in the water."
You “Nah guys. I cast the runes on paper, enchanting the paper. You put it on someone’s skin, wet it and hold it in place for 30 seconds. Bomb, temporary rune tattoo. Lasts 3-5 days” I say as I eat

Fred and George exchange a look of pure commercial awakening.

"Pre-printed. *Transferable*," George says slowly. "You're describing mass production."

"Which means the bottleneck isn't you at all," Fred says, doing rapid arithmetic in his head. "It's paper. We can enchant sheets in batches. We could do dozens a day."

"Right, so — throughput question." George leans in, suddenly businesslike. "Can you actually design one in, say, five minutes? Because I've got a bet with myself that you can."

"Test him," Fred says, eyes gleaming. "Right now. Winking lie-detector. If he does it in five minutes flat, I'll believe the galleon-a-pop queue is real."

Hermione, despite herself, has stopped eating. "A tattoo that *reacts to whether someone is lying*? That's — actually that's a nontrivial enchantment. Truth-detection is sworn-testimony grade magic."

"That," Fred says grandly, "is why we keep Press around."

All eyes turn to you.

I laugh “uh hermione is right. We could more easily make it react with the wearer lies. You want me to do that on someone right now? The paper is just the holder, I could do a temporary runic enchantment directly on someone”

"On someone, right now — though the paper's the smarter product, since it's batchable," you say. "But the lie-detector as described is too hard for a five-minute job. What we *can* do is have it react when the *wearer* lies. Different problem — the rune sits on the skin, keyed to the wearer's own speech. Much simpler."

"Same thing, innit?" Ron says through a mouthful of pie.

"It's really not," Hermione says, setting down her fork. "Detecting lies in *others* is sworn-testimony magic. Detecting your own — the rune's already on the body, keyed to the wearer. That's... actually feasible."

"Perfect test case either way," Fred says, scanning the table. "Who's got something to hide?"

"Ron," George and Harry say simultaneously.

"Oi!"

"Excellent," George says. "Weasley the control group. Press — do it. Right on his forearm. Then we interrogate him."

Ron holds out his arm with the resigned air of a man who's been an experimental subject before. "If it makes my arm fall off, I'm telling Mum about the swamp."
You “Test group!” I say cheerily as I begin to cast. The arcane energy forms the rune in the air then it lies itself on to Ron’s skin, resting then settling into a slightly glowing black blue design.

The rune settles into Ron's forearm like ink sinking into wet paper — a small, intricate design, black-blue, pulsing faintly once before going dormant.

"Oi, that's actually tidy," Ron says, turning his arm in the light. "Looks proper. Like something you'd pay for."

"That's the idea," Fred says. "Interrogation time. Ron. Is this pudding nice?"

"Very nice," Ron says promptly. The tattoo stays dark.

"Is Harry the best Seeker in this school?"

"Objectively, yes," Ron says. The rune stays dark. Harry looks pleased.

"Did you drop the Inkwell Charm assignment in second year and blame a ghost?"

Ron freezes. A half-second too long. "No," he says.

The tattoo *winks*. A distinct, unmissable flash of blue, right there on his forearm — and the table erupts.

"IT WORKS!" George slams the bench. "Three years, Ronald! Three years we took the blame for that!"

"That was Moaning Myrtle's fault!" Ron protests, and the tattoo winks again, twice, betraying him in real time. The table is howling. A few Ravenclaws at the next table along are craning their necks.

Hermione is watching the design closely, eyes sharp. "The trigger response is immediate. And it's catching *intent*, not just stated falsehoods — that second wink fired before he finished the sentence."

Fred turns to you, eyes gleaming like Galleons. "Press. How long to design that?"
You “I have a bunch of designs for random bullshit. Just need to put them on paper”

Fred stares at you. "You have a *stockpile*? Of finished designs?"

"He's not a stall," George says slowly, "he's a warehouse."

"Right. Okay." Fred pulls out a scrap of parchment, writing fast. "This weekend. We start the sheets — winking lie-detector first, everyone will pay double to catch a mate lying. Then whatever else you've got."

"Fred," Hermione says, in her precise warning tone, "that tattoo is doing genuine body-bound conditional work. If Ravenclaws start asking how it's constructed—"

"Then we charge them for the answer," Fred says sweetly.

Harry leans in, grinning. "Can I be labour? I want in on this."
You “The Press Sigils Tattoos in collaboration with Weasleys Wheezes” I grin

"'The Press Sigils Tattoos in collaboration with Weasleys' Wheezes,'" George repeats, savoring it. "Has a ring. 'Press & Wheezes.' 'Sigils & Sneakoscopes'—"

"We'll workshop it," Fred says, already writing. "Harry's in as labour, pending terms. Sheets by the weekend." He glances up. "And speaking of which — you, workshop, after dinner tonight. Bring the stockpile list."

Hermione taps your arm, quieter, nodding toward the next table. "Ravenclaws are still watching. That tattoo did conditional-trigger work in front of thirty people. Word will spread by dinner — you'd better decide what you're selling and what you're keeping before someone clever starts asking questions."

Ron, meanwhile, is scratching at his forearm. "How do I get this thing off?"
I laugh at Ron “bro I told you, 3-5 days. Just cover it like an adult.” I tell hermione, Fred and George “let them masses wonder. We work tonight!”

"'Cover it like an adult,'" Ron repeats, betrayed, as the twins cackle.

"Tonight," Fred says, saluting you with his goblet. "Workshop, after dinner. Bring the list."

"Bring *extra* of whatever made that rune wink," George adds. "We'll want stockpile priorities."

Hermione just shakes her head, but she's smiling into her food. "You're all going to end up in detention. I'm saying that now, for the record."

Harry leans back, arms crossed, thoroughly entertained. "So this is what I've been missing. Last year was all Hogsmeade trips and homework."

Across the Hall, you catch sight of the Slytherin table — Draconia's head turns briefly toward your group, then away, expression unreadable. Whatever she's heard, word travels fast.

cards.title: Seth Press — Arcane Sigil Tattoos
cards.content:
Appearance: An elaborate, interconnected blackwork tattoo system extending from Seth’s left ribs across his chest and back, over his right shoulder, and down his arm in a three-quarter sleeve. The design resembles intricate sacred geometry blended with mathematical notation: nested circles, intersecting lines, precise angles, branching pathways, and hundreds of smaller sigils. Active sections glow with arcane light during casting.

Purpose: The tattoos contain no spells. Instead, they provide reusable foundational magical functions that assist Seth with virtually any form of spellwork.

Foundational functions. 

Ground: Establishes a stable reference point for magical energy flow.

Anchor: Fixes a magical working to a chosen physical reference.

Channel: Directs magical energy along a selected pathway or structure.

Gather: Collects magical energy from available sources for controlled use.

Meter: Regulates precisely how much magical energy enters a working.

Split: Divides a single magical flow into separate controlled pathways.

Merge: Combines multiple compatible magical flows into one unified stream.

Gate: Opens or closes designated pathways within a magical working.

Isolate: Prevents unwanted interactions between separate magical energies or structures.

Contain: Restricts magical energy or effects within specifically defined boundaries.

Shape: Defines the geometric structure and boundaries of magical effects.

Bind: Attaches magical effects to designated objects, targets, or locations.

Stabilize: Maintains the structural integrity and coherence of magical workings.

Sustain: Supports the continued operation of adequately powered magical effects.

Delay: Controls the timing of a magical effect’s eventual activation.

Trigger: Initiates magical operations when specified conditions have been satisfied.

Detect: Identifies predefined magical conditions, changes, signatures, or external influences.

Feedback: Returns information about a working’s current state and performance.

Convert: Transforms compatible magical inputs into other usable energy configurations.

Discharge: Directs accumulated or residual magical energy toward designated outlets.

Integration: Every sigil is carefully designed to work with the others. Their interconnected geometry forms a cohesive, modular magical framework. Seth can combine and activate different functions as needed, supporting spellcasting without replacing the spells themselves. The system is exceptionally elegant, versatile, and efficient.

Design Philosophy: Seth deliberately selected fundamental magical principles rather than specialized techniques. These functions are basic and universal enough that future magical discoveries are unlikely to render them obsolete. Equivalent sigils can be drawn with chalk, ink, or other conventional methods; the tattoos make them permanently accessible and beautifully integrated.

Unintended Side Effect: Years of channeling magic through this extensive network have gradually caused magic to become integrated into Seth’s living body itself. Neither Seth nor other researchers currently understand the full implications. This transformation is subtle, largely undiscovered, and its eventual consequences remain unknown.

Established Properties: The tattoos are functional, convenient, visually striking, and deliberately showy. They provide genuine casting advantages without introducing inherent disadvantages. Their full interconnected design is far more sophisticated than any individual foundational sigil.

CURRENT CAPABILITY: Seth already possesses this complete, functional network as part of his fourth-year skill set. The tattoos contain reusable primitives, not fixed spells; they improve casting without replacing learned spell design. In a 2 September library demonstration, Seth enhanced a Constringo binding tether by funneling magic through these sigils for controlled flow and greater effect; this was ordinary rune-assisted casting, not use of recursive feedback. Seth's separate open-air recursion demonstration routed magic through his tattoos but did not establish that the tattoos solve, stop or stabilize a runaway recursive loop. Draconia has seen their outward effects and identified some visible gating/metering patterns, not learned their full internal architecture. The subtle integration with Seth's living body remains largely unexplored, with no established inherent downside.

cards.title: Rune Engineering — Seth’s Specialty
cards.content: Runes are a sophisticated branch of high-ceiling magical engineering, not cosmetic glowing symbols or weak preparatory spells. A competent array encodes precise conditions, geometry, feedback, routing, timing, targeting, protections and persistent operations. Mastery can support startlingly powerful enchantments, adaptive wards, magical logic and conditional spell behavior. Seth is already an advanced practitioner, not a novice discovering that runes exist. He can deploy arrays via gesture, inscribed surfaces, temporary constructs or his integrated sigil tattoos, depending on the working. Tattoos implement foundational reusable functions; they do not replace spell design. New mechanisms require discovery, but no arbitrary nerfs or universal rune counters. On 2 September Seth diagnosed and repaired an unstable Fainting Fancy Mark IV by carving a feed/meter/stabilize rune; one successful test followed, not a completed production run. Later he visibly enhanced a Constringo tether with reusable tattoo functions alone, separate from the tenth-circumstance recursion research. Witnesses may observe effects without understanding construction.

cards.title: Fred and George — Active Magical Products, September 2001
cards.content: Fred and George's current magical joke projects include Skiving Snackboxes (Fainting Fancies and Nosebleed Noughts), a previously unstable Portable Swamp concept, extendable ears, and experimental Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder modifications. The twins work in a concealed workshop near Gryffindor Tower's upper corridors. Fainting Fancy Mark IV initially had a severe flow mismatch between its trigger and containment, making the intended faint unreliable. Seth inspected its magical structure with floating sigils and carved a subtle feed/meter/stabilize array into the product housing. Fred tested the modified version and briefly fainted as intended; that single demonstration succeeded, though no batch-level reliability evidence yet exists. Seth proposed template-based mass enchanting to supply inventory, but no actual production run or sales have occurred on-screen. Seth also suggested binding the swamp with controllable containment and recall; that design remains unbuilt and untested. Lee Jordan agreed to five percent of the Portable Swamp fund, not an ownership share in every product.
